name: restic-mediafire-backup
objective: Create and maintain an encrypted restic backup of /home/ukhan/claude_ukhan and /home/ukhan/gemini in the MediaFire account, using the MediaFire FUSE mount at /media/mediafire and the restic repository at /media/mediafire/backup.

status.first_real_backup_attempt: failed 2026-11-08T18:35:21+03:00 on data/68: rename ... no such file or directory. It was the asynchronous release/rename race, not a data problem: 15 packs were uploaded but no snapshot was created.
status.second_real_backup_attempt: failed 2026-11-08T22:21:40+03:00 on data/fd: same rename race. patched4 only waited up to 60 s for a device/get_changes() refresh to publish the temp file; on a real multi-pack run that refresh lagged, so the kernel rename lookup returned ENOENT and mediafirefs_rename() was never called.
status.fix: 0.60+patched5 publishes a freshly uploaded file deterministically: mediafirefs_release() reloads just the parent directory with folder/get_content (folder_tree_reload_dir()), which reflects the new file immediately, instead of waiting for device/get_changes(). mediafirefs_mkdir() reloads its parent too, and mediafirefs_rename() updates the local name directly. patched1-4 are retained. A 286 MiB multi-pack restic backup (snapshot 4def8015, tag p5-test) passed with zero FUSE rename/upload errors.
status.orphan_packs: The packs from the failed attempts were indexed with restic rebuild-index (18 packs total) and restic check is clean; the restarted backup deduplicated instead of re-uploading. The unreferenced packs and the forgotten test-snapshot packs were removed by an explicit restic prune on 2026-11-08 (see prune_result).

restic_password.location: embedded directly in restic-mediafire-backup.sh, as required
restic_password.warning: The script is a secret. Do not commit it, copy it to a world-readable location, or paste its contents into public logs.

mediafire_account.note: The MediaFire username/password live in the mediafire-tools config and are used by mediafire-fuse and mediafire-shell. They are not duplicated in the backup script.

session_tokens.where: mediafire-fuse writes signed MediaFire API URLs, which include session tokens, to stderr
session_tokens.mitigation: The FUSE log is mode 600 under the state directory and must be deleted after troubleshooting.

mount.install_method: apt-get install --reinstall /home/ukhan/gemini/opi4a/crosscompile/mediafire-tools_0.60+patched5_arm64.deb (dpkg status ii; apt candidate 0.60+patched5)
mount.forbidden_reason: The FUSE filesystem does not implement statfs; stat -f and df fail even when the mount is healthy.
mount.wait_behavior: Poll mountpoint -q plus a root-directory readdir once per second. The daemon daemonizes, so the parent process exiting is not a mount failure.

repository.backend: restic local backend on the MediaFire FUSE mount

layout.precreation_method: MediaFire API via mediafire-shell, before restic init
layout.precreation_reason: Each FUSE mkdir triggers a remote folder lookup/tree refresh; creating 256 data subdirs through FUSE was slow and prone to API stalls. Pre-creating the layout avoids 256 slow mkdir operations during restic init.

storage.estimated_repository_size: less than the 3.8 GiB source size because restic compresses and deduplicates
storage.monitor: Check MediaFire storage after the first backup; prune/clean old snapshots if needed.

flags.one_file_system: Do not cross filesystem boundaries inside the source trees.
flags.skip_if_unchanged: Skip creating a new snapshot when the source is unchanged since the matching parent snapshot.

backup.pack_size: default 16 MiB; the patched FUSE transfer timeout is 900 seconds to accommodate slow MediaFire uploads
backup.duration_estimate: The 2 MiB smoke backup took 43 seconds. The real 3.8 GiB run depends on MediaFire upload bandwidth; at the observed ~50 KiB/s it can take roughly 20+ hours. Run it in the background and monitor the log.

exit_codes.3: some source files could not be read; a snapshot may still have been created

retention.reason: Pruning over the FUSE mount is slow, reads/deletes many pack files, and MediaFire moves deleted files to trash. It is opt-in so the default backup run cannot accidentally remove data.
retention.caution: Prune deletes unreferenced packs. Verify with restic check before/after. Empty the MediaFire trash from the web UI if deleted packs accumulate there.

smoke_test.notes: The smoke backup used the same restic repository and the same patched FUSE mount. It proves init, backup, snapshot listing, full read-data check, restore, and remote pack visibility.

rename_race_test.notes: A single-pack test that passed under patched4. It did NOT exercise the multi-pack rollout where the device/get_changes() refresh lagged; the real backup then failed again at 22:21:40. The snapshot was forgotten on 2026-11-08.

multi_pack_test.notes: Exercises ~18 data packs plus lock/index files, i.e. many create -> write -> close -> release(upload) -> rename cycles in one run. This is the scenario that defeated patched4. Snapshot 4def8015 was forgotten on 2026-11-08.

real_backup_result.notes: The real backup of /home/ukhan/claude_ukhan and /home/ukhan/gemini completed under patched5 with no recurrences of the earlier rename race.

restore_sample.notes: End-to-end retrieval check: reads pack data back over the FUSE mount and compares byte-for-byte. A full-tree restore is intentionally avoided (slow over FUSE); the smoke test already restored a full tree.

prerequisites: Network access to MediaFire and the mediafire-tools patched FUSE binary (or another way to expose the repository)
steps: Mount the MediaFire account: mountpoint -q /media/mediafire || nohup /usr/bin/mediafire-fuse /media/mediafire >> /tmp/mediafire-fuse-recovery.log 2>&1 &
Wait until mountpoint -q /media/mediafire and timeout 10 ls /media/mediafire succeeds.
Set RESTIC_PASSWORD to the value embedded in restic-mediafire-backup.sh.
Run restic restore latest --target /tmp/restic-restore --host orangepi-4a --tag mediafire.
Compare the restored tree with the source, or restore only the needed paths.
recovery.full_repository_copy: If MediaFire is unavailable, the repository can be copied while mounted with rsync -a /media/mediafire/backup/ /some/local/restic-repo/ (slow over FUSE).

patched_fuse.build: Native aarch64 build with GCC 15.2 and CMake 4; CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5 was required, and -Werror was removed because GCC 15 emits new warnings in the 0.60 sources. Build tree was /tmp/opencode/mf-src/build-aarch64. Rebuild after re-cloning upstream and re-applying the patches below.

patches.name: folder_tree_housekeep disabled
patches.reason: The cached tree can contain a dangling, non-NULL parent pointer. folder_tree_is_parent_of() then dereferences it and the daemon SIGSEGVs during the optional housekeeping pass. The pass now returns immediately.

patches.name: fsync and fsyncdir return success
patches.reason: The original callbacks returned -ENOSYS. restic calls fsync on files and directories and aborts on that error. Uploads are performed synchronously in release(), so reporting success is correct for this workflow.

patches.name: bounded HTTP timeouts
patches.reason: The original libcurl calls had no total timeout, so one stuck MediaFire API request blocked the whole single-mutex filesystem indefinitely. GET requests now time out after 30 seconds; other transfers (including uploads) after 900 seconds; low-speed transfers abort after 60 seconds below 1 KiB/s.

patches.name: readdir offset patch attempted and reverted
patches.reason: Passing offset cookies to filldir caused EIO and a hung mount on this FUSE 2.9/kernel combination. The patch was reverted. The remaining limitation is cosmetic for restic: coreutils ls on a 256-entry directory such as backup/data can hang, while Python os.listdir(), restic's Go readdir, and stat on individual entries work.

patches.name: rename waits for asynchronous release (0.60+patched2)
patches.reason: restic close()s a temp file and immediately rename()s it; mediafirefs_release() uploads asynchronously, so the old path has no remote key yet. mediafirefs_rename() now waits up to 1000 s for folder_tree_path_get_key(oldpath), dropping ctx->mutex while sleeping so the release worker can run.

patches.name: rename API retry with key re-lookup (0.60+patched3)
patches.reason: mfconn_api_file_update()/mfconn_api_folder_update() failed intermittently while the upload was still in flight. mediafirefs_rename() retries 20x5 s, re-resolving the key each round. The script also runs the daemon with -f so post-start API errors reach the FUSE log, and a folderkey == NULL comparison bug was fixed.

patches.name: keep temp path visible during upload (0.60+patched4, retained)
patches.reason: release() removed the temp path from ctx->sv_writefiles at the start, but getattr() uses that vector to report a not-yet-uploaded temp path as a regular file. Between that removal and the tree refresh, the kernel's rename lookup returned ENOENT and mediafirefs_rename() was never called (which is why locks sometimes worked and the index failed). patched4 keeps the entry for the whole upload and removes it on every error path. Its 60 s wait for folder_tree_path_is_file() was not enough on a real multi-pack run, so patched5 replaces that wait.

patches.name: deterministic upload/rename publication (0.60+patched5)
patches.reason: After a successful upload, mediafirefs_release() reloads just the parent directory with folder/get_content (new public folder_tree_reload_dir()), which reflects the new file immediately, instead of waiting for the unreliable device/get_changes() refresh. mediafirefs_mkdir() reloads its parent after folder/create so a new folder key is available to the next upload. mediafirefs_rename() keeps the patched2 wait and patched3 retries, fixes the folderkey == NULL check, and syncs the local tree name directly via the new folder_tree_rename_entry() instead of a full folder_tree_update(true). The two whole-tree folder_tree_debug() dumps in folder_tree_update() were removed (the FUSE log had grown to ~7 MB per run). patched1-4 are retained.

known_limitations: The MediaFire FUSE filesystem is not a fully POSIX-compliant filesystem and is not an enterprise backup backend.

Reading a file immediately after renaming it in the same mount can return EPERM because the in-memory file cache revision is stale. Unmounting and remounting fixes it. The smoke backup, snapshot listing, read-data check, and restore all succeeded; the script remounts and retries the repository config read if needed.

coreutils ls on the 256-entry backup/data directory can hang due to the readdir cookie limitation. Do not use ls on huge repo directories; use python3 -c 'import os; print(len(os.listdir(...)))' or restic itself.
fsync/fsyncdir are no-ops; the actual durability point is the upload in release(). Always verify with restic check.
Tree housekeeping is disabled, so stale cache entries are not automatically pruned. Remount periodically or delete the mediafire-tools cache if the tree looks wrong.
The FUSE daemon serializes operations with one mutex; a long upload blocks other filesystem operations.
MediaFire API requests can still fail or be rate-limited even with timeouts. Rerun the backup; restic deduplicates and resumes.
The MediaFire account had about 20.8 GiB free before the first backup. The repository must fit; monitor storage and prune old snapshots if necessary.
The restic password is embedded in the script, so the script is a secret. The FUSE log contains session tokens. Keep both at mode 600/700 and delete the FUSE log after troubleshooting.
The backup is a point-in-time snapshot. Files modified during the backup can cause restic exit code 3; rerun to capture a clean snapshot.
MediaFire's trash retains deleted files. Prune/folder deletion may require emptying the trash from the MediaFire web UI.

failure_modes_and_mitigations.mitigation: Script starts the patched binary and waits for mountpoint + root readdir.
Script attempts a normal unmount, then lazy unmount, kills the stale daemon, and remounts.

failure_modes_and_mitigations.detection: FUSE request or restic operation stalls
failure_modes_and_mitigations.mitigation: Patched binary limits GETs to 30 seconds and other transfers to 900 seconds; low-speed transfers abort after 60 seconds. Retry the script.

failure_modes_and_mitigations.detection: restic backup returns nonzero or restic check reports missing packs
failure_modes_and_mitigations.mitigation: Rerun the backup; restic reuses existing packs and retries missing data. Check the FUSE log.

failure_modes_and_mitigations.detection: restic reports permission denied reading a repository file
failure_modes_and_mitigations.mitigation: Unmount/remount; the script retries the repository config read and the check once after a remount.

failure_modes_and_mitigations.detection: coreutils ls on a 256-entry directory stalls
failure_modes_and_mitigations.mitigation: Use Python os.listdir or restic; avoid ls on huge repository directories. This does not affect restic's own readdir.
The board had ~128 GiB free. Clean ~/.cache/mediafire-tools and ~/.cache/restic if needed.

failure_modes_and_mitigations.detection: MediaFire API error or storage_limit_exceeded flag
failure_modes_and_mitigations.mitigation: Free space, prune old snapshots, or empty trash from the web UI. The account had ~20.8 GiB free.
Script mode 700, state dir mode 700, FUSE log mode 600. Delete the FUSE log after troubleshooting.

summary: Installed mediafire-tools 0.60+patched5 (patched FUSE binary). The older debs (original 0.60, patched1/2/3/4) were flushed at the user's request; only the patched5 deb is kept.
Created /media/mediafire/backup and its restic layout through the MediaFire API to avoid 256 slow FUSE mkdir calls.
Mounted the patched FUSE binary and ran restic init; repository id 6a2ca84e74.
Ran a 2 MiB smoke backup, restic check --read-data, and a restore/diff; all passed.

The first two real backups failed on the asynchronous release/rename race; patched4 fixed the single-pack case but not a multi-pack run. patched5 makes publication deterministic. A 300 MB multi-pack test (snapshot 4def8015) then passed with zero FUSE errors.
one_time_setup.mediafire_shell_note: The one-time layout creation used mediafire-shell with a temporary config file. The MediaFire password contains a # character; shlex with comments=False is required. The shell reads ./.mediafire-tools.conf from its working directory (the upstream code has a homedir-path bug), so run it from a private directory containing that file. Do not leave that temporary config behind.

first_real_backup.note: Run in the background. The first real backup is the long one; later runs use --skip-if-unchanged and are fast when nothing changed.

daily_or_manual_backup.note: The script leaves the FUSE mount mounted and reuses it on the next run.

deep_verification.note: Reads 10% of pack data and verifies hashes.

prune.note: Opt-in. Remounts before forget --prune. Can be slow and moves deleted packs to MediaFire trash.

restore.command: mountpoint -q /media/mediafire || nohup /usr/bin/mediafire-fuse /media/mediafire >> /tmp/mf-restore.log 2>&1 & sleep 5; export RESTIC_REPOSITORY=/media/mediafire/backup; export RESTIC_PASSWORD='<from script>'; restic restore latest --target /tmp/restic-restore --host orangepi-4a --tag mediafire
restore.note: Use the password embedded in restic-mediafire-backup.sh. Restore to a scratch directory first.

scheduling.systemd_timer: Create a oneshot service running the script and a timer with OnCalendar=daily; ensure the service runs as ukhan and has HOME set.
scheduling.caution: Do not schedule prune and backup at the same time; the script's flock prevents concurrent runs, but a long first backup may overlap the next scheduled run.

temporary_files_to_remove: any temporary .mediafire-tools.conf you create (remove after use)
